answer_1.quote: Abstractive summarization aims to generate a concise summary that contains the critical information of the source text while ensuring the generated text is fluent and faithful.

answer_2.quote: Then, we investigate the human correlations of two popular faithfulness evaluation metrics, FactCC and QAFactEval, on future data.

answer_4.quote: We conduct extensive human evaluations to annotate the types of hallucinations made by system-generated summaries. Four authors from this paper annotate the above model-generated summaries.
answer_4.guideline: For each generated summary, we first decide whether the sentence is faithful, i.e., the information can be entailed by the source article. If it is not faithful, we verify it through Wikipedia to decide whether they are factual to world knowledge at the time the article was published or outdated if it could be connected to the knowledge from the past. If there is no information found to support the unfaithful entities, then labeled as non-verifiable errors.
